In wake-up stroke the time of onset is unknown: what counts is the last time the patient was seen well (here 9.5 hours earlier). Non-contrast CT excludes blood and looks for early ischaemic signs: loss of the insular ribbon, blurring of the basal ganglia, cortical hypodensity and less visible sulci. ASPECTS divides the middle cerebral artery territory into 10 regions (caudate, lentiform, internal capsule, insula, M1-M3 at the basal ganglia level, M4-M6 above) and subtracts one point for each affected region: here insula, M1 and M4, so about 7. With ASPECTS 6 or more and a large-vessel occlusion on CT angiography, thrombectomy is possible beyond 6 hours (up to 24 hours with selection criteria); thrombolysis beyond 4.5 hours requires selection with MRI or perfusion.
Use the arterial territory atlas after answering: the hypodensity falls in the frontal and insular territories of the left middle cerebral artery.
